names.note: saint.gr writes the name in Latin letters in its line for 28 Μαρτίου, «Άγιος Boyan ο επονομαζόμενος Enravota πρίγκιπας των Βουλγάρων», and gives its own Greek renderings in brackets in the body, «ο Άγιος Boyan (Μποϋάν) ο επονομαζόμενος Enravota (Ενραβωτά)». Those bracketed forms are the only Greek ones the page prints.
The second of the two bracketed Greek forms on the same page; it renders the byname the page gives as Enravota.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's fourth heading for the Julian 28 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Свети мученик Бојан, кнез бугарски.“, with Свети left off, which is not a rank, with the rank word мученик left off, and with кнез бугарски left off as well, which is the office. The heading gives no second name — the Enravota this folder carries from saint.gr is not on the page — so the bare forename is what the source gives; no other folder in the corpus holds a Serbian Бојан.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 28ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Boyan ο επονομαζόμενος Enravota πρίγκιπας των Βουλγάρων»

attestations.note: The page makes him the eldest son of Omurtag, king of Bulgaria from 816 to 831, passed over for the throne in favour of his younger brother Malamir; it puts the beheading «περί το έτος 833 μ.Χ.» and cites Theophylact, archbishop of Ochrid from 1090 to 1126, for the prophecy it quotes. It prints no hymn and names no relic.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 10.04.2026 (28. март ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Бојан, кнез бугарски.“

attestations.note: The day's fourth entry, on the same menologion day the Greek already keeps in this folder, and the same prince of the Bulgars, beheaded at his own brother's order for confessing Christ. **It dates the beheading 827 where this folder holds about 833 from saint.gr**, and 827 falls outside that; the sourced year is left standing and the disagreement is recorded here rather than resolved. It gives the family the Greek page did not: his father Krutogon, his grandfather Gruboš, and the brother who gave the order, Milomir, who was a heathen. None of the three was read as any folder in this corpus and none takes a row. The stored form is the bare forename, because Свети is not a rank and мученик and кнез бугарски are the rank and the office this folder keeps in `types`; Enravota, the second name this folder carries from saint.gr, is nowhere on the Prologue's page. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: saint.gr: «ο βασιλέας διέταξε τον διά αποκεφαλισμού θάνατό του. Ήταν περί το έτος 833 μ.Χ.» — the page's «περί», about, is why the display says about 833. It gives no year of birth.
